title: Rose-type gate — is this rose a supported bush-rose type?

common.applies_to: Any rose a gardener brings to the pruning journey. This prerequisite check runs before every other gate and every observation, dead wood included.
common.preserved_uncertainty: (1) Pip can't tell a rose's type from photos or a dormant plant (AF-20, R-1). The gate relies entirely on what the gardener has been told. (2) Some cultivars are classed differently by different authorities (ARC §4, AF-5), so a stated type isn't infallible. (3) Grandiflora is included provisionally only. It's largely absent from NZ classification sources (AF-4), and Pip gives no Grandiflora-specific pruning guidance (R-4). (4) "Ht" and "Fl" are shop abbreviations that no source spells out; their meaning was shown by matching five Kings Plant Barn roses against nurseries that name the class in full (AF-L30, AF-L32). One Palmers title uses "Ht" on a rose its own page calls a Floribunda (AF-L31), so the hint says "usually". Either way the rose qualifies.

content.question: Do you know what type of rose this is — from its label or pot tag, a receipt or nursery listing, or someone experienced who has told you?

labelAbbreviations.text: Don't rely on "Ht" or "Fl" in a rose's name to tell you its type: one New Zealand shop sells a rose as "Ht" that its own page describes as a Floribunda.

answers.label: Another type (shrub, English, patio, miniature, groundcover, climbing or rambling, standard, old garden or species rose)
The label only says "bush rose" or "rose bush"
I know its variety name but not its type

content.grandifloraNote: Grandiflora is supported provisionally. It gets the same guidance as a Hybrid Tea; there is no Grandiflora-specific advice.

roseFinder.text: The New Zealand Rose Society's Rose Finder lists a type for each rose it holds. Look the name up there, then answer this question again. If you can't find it, the answer is the same as "I don't know".

journalOnly.base: I can't yet help prune this rose. My pruning guidance so far covers only Hybrid Tea, Floribunda and Grandiflora bush roses.
journalOnly.excluded: That type isn't one my pruning guidance covers yet.
journalOnly.bushOnly: "Bush" on a label doesn't always say which type a rose is. At least one New Zealand nursery calls a shrub rose a "bush" rose.
journalOnly.unknown: Without a confirmed type I can't be sure the guidance fits. I don't try to identify roses from photos, because telling one rose from another is difficult and depends on many parts of the plant.
journalOnly.keep: Your rose stays in your garden list as a journal: photos, notes and history all remain available. If you later confirm it is a Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora, you can answer this question again.
journalOnly.help: If you want the type identified, a local rose society or an experienced rose grower can help.
